claims.text: The starting material is selective-laser-melted Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy.
The as-printed alloy has a single-FCC cellular microstructure.
The as-printed alloy has a uniform Cr distribution and lacks nanoprecipitates.
Uniform Cr distribution in the as-printed state enables prompt formation of a continuous protective Cr2O3 scale.
Aging at 750°C for 50 hours induces approximately 25–30 vol% Ni/Ti-enriched L12 nanoscale precipitates.
The aging treatment also induces larger Al/Ti-enriched and Cr/Fe-depleted L21 precipitates concentrated at cell walls.
Cr-depleted precipitates, especially L21 precipitates, retard establishment of a continuous protective Cr2O3 scale.
The increased matrix–precipitate interface density disrupts the formation and continuity of the Cr2O3 layer.
Precipitate–matrix interfaces provide short-circuit diffusion paths that increase oxygen or reactive-species ingress.
Delayed formation of a continuous Cr2O3 layer produces a thicker and less coherent duplex-to-trilayer oxide scale.
Enhanced ingress promotes development of a thicker inner Al/Ti-rich oxide region.
Internal stresses associated with the multilayer oxide scale cause microcracking during extended exposure.
Microcracking promotes oxide spallation and can ultimately trigger catastrophic failure.
Relative to the as-printed alloy, the aged alloy will exhibit greater oxidation mass gain.
Relative to the as-printed alloy, the aged alloy will form a thicker and less protective oxide scale.
The aged alloy will develop a more pronounced inner Al/Ti-rich oxide region, particularly above 900°C.
The aged alloy will show more microcracking and spallation than the as-printed baseline.
The proposed behavior applies from 600°C to 1200°C for exposure durations up to 96 hours, with marked effects above 900°C.
The proposed degradation mechanism operates under both oxidizing and reducing gas exposures.
Under high-temperature reducing conditions, microstructural inhomogeneities and crack propagation contribute to catastrophic failure.
